newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk management spokesman plays down strike talk.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk management spokesman plays down strike talk.

text.p: A RAO Norilsk Nickel spokesman said on Wednesday that he did not think workers at the flagship metals plant would strike on March 15 and said that a trade union leader's talk of disrupting output was premature.
"I don't think it will go to this," Moscow-based Norilsk spokesman Anatoly Komrakov said. "We will do everything possible to make it so that there is no strike."
Boris Degtyaryov, deputy head of the Norilsk plant's United Trade Union committee, was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying that workers might strike on March 15 over salary and other arrears.
Komrakov also said Norilsk's January convertor matte nickel output rose 8.6 percent on December 1996 and 8.8 percent year-on-year, but he gave no absolute production volumes.
January cobalt production rose 12.1 percent month-on-month and 2.2 percent year-on-year, while January copper rose 1.0 percent on December 1996 and 2.2 percent on January 1996.
January ore mining increased 7.0 percent month-on-month and 9.8 percent year-on-year.

Komrakov said tax police officials in the Arctic town of Norilsk, where the main plant is based, were struggling to sell about 625 billion roubles' worth of various metals. Tax police seized and released the metal earlier this month, but a quarrel ensued over who would sell the metal, Komrakov said.
Workers were attempting to block the sales, Komrakov said, since proceeds from sales by the tax police would go to the regional Krasnoyarsk budget rather than to pay off salary and other arrears.

He said workers at the flagship mining and metallurgical complex had last been fully paid for October 1996 and total salary arrears and overdue holiday payments had come down over an unspecified period to 900 billion roubles from 1.2 trillion.
The Norilsk Nickel group also owes about 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets, he said.

Komrakov said an independent arbitration court, whose decisions have no legally-binding force but to which aggrieved parties can turn with disputes, was examining workers' complaints and would take a decision on Wednesday.
RAO Norilsk Nickel is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt, and platinum group metals to world markets. --Lynnley Browning, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
